Practical Content:
1. Identify the longer leg (anode) and shorter leg (cathode) of the LED.
2. Connect the LED and a resistor on the breadboard.
3. Connect them to the Arduino.
4. Write a simple program to make the LED blink.
5. Change the delay time to see how fast it blinks!

1. Connect 2 or more LEDs to the Arduino.
2. Write code to blink them one by one or together.
3. Try making fun patterns like a traffic light or running lights.
4. Learn how to control multiple lights at the same time!

1. Connect a push button to the Arduino.
2. Learn how the button sends "pressed" (HIGH) or "not pressed" (LOW) signals.
3. Write code to check if the button is pressed.
4. See the button's status on your computer screen!

1. Connect both an LED and a push button to the Arduino.
2. Write a program to turn the LED ON when you press the button.
3. Make the LED turn OFF when you let go.
4. Try making the button act like a switch to turn the LED on and off!

Tab: Four LEDs Controlled by Two Buttons
Practical Content:
1. Connect 4 LEDs and 2 push buttons.
2. Program one button to make the lights move forward.
3. Program the other button to make them move backward.
4. Have fun creating different light patterns!

1. Connect a small speaker (buzzer) to the Arduino.
2. Write code to make it play sounds.
3. Change the numbers in the code to hear different pitches (high or low sounds).
4. Try making it play a simple song or a warning beep!

1. Connect a small screen (LCD) to the Arduino.
2. Learn how to adjust the screen brightness.
3. Write code to display your name or a fun message on the screen.
4. See how screens show information!

1. Connect an LCD screen, a buzzer, and 2 buttons.
2. Use one button to make the sound higher and the other to make it lower.
3. Show the sound level on the screen.
4. Combine everything you've learned into one cool project!

1. Look at all the parts for your RoboCar (motors, wheels, battery, etc.).
2. Learn what each part does.
3. Understand how the "brain" (Arduino) tells the wheels to move using a special helper (motor driver).

1. Learn how a motor spins forward and backward.
2. Change the wires to see the motor spin in the opposite direction.
3. Understand how the Arduino sends signals to change the spin direction.

Tab: Interfacing Two DC Motors with L293D
Practical Content:
1. Connect two motors to the motor driver helper.
2. Test the left motor and the right motor.
3. Test both motors at the same time.
4. Learn how to control two wheels for your RoboCar!

Tab: Basic RoboCar Movement: Forward and Backward
Practical Content:
1. Attach the motors and wheels to the RoboCar body.
2. Write a program to make the car move forward and backward.
3. Make sure both wheels spin the right way so the car goes straight.
4. Watch your RoboCar drive!
